I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize system and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I have only 10.1 mu and 2 people in the household, so I need a plan that is steady, familiar, and not too hard to manage. After 40 years of farming, I trust the wheat-maize rotation most on my irrigated land because it gives me stable grain output and makes full use of the year. I will put 8.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields, and I will keep 2.0 mu in cotton so I still have some cash-crop income without making field work too scattered. I will use better seed, not old traditional seed, because I want even emergence and stable yield. Since I have well irrigation, I will water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. I will not push fertilizer to extremes; I will use moderate, familiar rates that match my land and my labor. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits my scale. I will spray when needed to keep weeds, insects, and disease under control, but I will keep it to the number of passes I think are necessary. My goal this year is stable production, manageable field work, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
